items.stem: What is the three-figure bearing of north-east?
items.markingKey: North-east is halfway between north (000°) and east (090°).

items.stem: Explain why a bearing of 45° is written as 045°.
items.answer: Bearings are always written with three figures so that they cannot be misread; zeros fill the empty places.
items.markingKey: B1 three figures convention; B1 avoids misreading [2]

items.stem: Explain why the bearing of A from B differs from the bearing of B from A by 180°.
items.answer: The two directions are opposite along the same line; the north lines at A and B are parallel, so the angles differ by 180° (co-interior/alternate angles).
items.markingKey: B1 opposite directions; B1 parallel north lines [2]

items.stem: A map has a scale of 1 : 20,000. A straight road is 3.6 km long. Calculate the length of the road on the map, in centimetres.
A map has a scale of 1 : 200,000. A straight road is 1.2 km long. Calculate the length of the road on the map, in centimetres.

A boat leaves harbour H and sails 20 km on a bearing of 040° to a buoy B. It then sails 25 km on a bearing of 130° to an island I. The angle HBI is 90°. (a) Write down the bearing of H from B. (b) Calculate the bearing of I from H.
A map scale is 1 : 25 000. Explain why 1 cm on the map represents 250 m.
items.answer: 1 cm on the map represents 25 000 cm in real life, and 25 000 cm = 250 m.
items.markingKey: B1 25 000 cm; B1 convert to 250 m [2]

items.stem: Describe how to draw a bearing of 230° from a point P on a scale drawing.
items.answer: Draw a north line at P, place the protractor on P and measure 230° clockwise from north (180° + 50°), then draw the line.
items.markingKey: B1 north line at P; B1 clockwise 230° [2]

items.stem: A map has a scale of 1 : 10,000. A straight road is 12 km long. Calculate the length of the road on the map, in centimetres.
A map has a scale of 1 : 25,000. A straight road is 7 km long. Calculate the length of the road on the map, in centimetres.

A boat leaves harbour H and sails 24 km on a bearing of 150° to a buoy B. It then sails 25 km on a bearing of 060° to an island I. The angle HBI is 90°. (a) Calculate the bearing of H from I. (b) A chart of the area has scale 1 : 500,000. Calculate the length of HB on the chart.
In a right-angled triangle, sin θ is equal to
items.markingKey: SOH: sin = opp/hyp.

items.stem: Explain why sin θ can never be greater than 1 in a right-angled triangle.
items.answer: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse and the hypotenuse is always the longest side, so the fraction is less than 1.
items.markingKey: B1 definition; B1 hypotenuse longest [2]

items.stem: Explain how you decide which trigonometric ratio to use to find a missing side.
items.answer: Label the sides relative to the given angle; choose the ratio that uses the side you know and the side you want (SOH CAH TOA).
items.markingKey: B1 label opp/adj/hyp; B1 choose ratio containing known and unknown [2]

items.stem: In a right-angled triangle, one angle is 51° and the side adjacent to the angle is 11 cm. Calculate the length of the side opposite the angle.
In a right-angled triangle, one angle is 72° and the side opposite the angle is 6 cm. Calculate the length of the side adjacent to the angle.
In a right-angled triangle, one angle is 74.4° and the side adjacent to the angle is 20.3 cm. Calculate the length of the side opposite the angle.

Yusuf flies a kite on a straight string of length 30 m on a beach near Riyadh. The string makes an angle of 47° with the horizontal, and Yusuf holds it 1.5 m above the ground. (a) Calculate the horizontal distance from the hand to the point directly below the kite. (b) The string is let out to 1.5 times its length at the same angle. Explain what happens to the height of the kite above the hand.
items.answer: (a) 20.5 m (b) It is multiplied by 1.5, since height = length × sin θ and the angle is unchanged.

items.markingKey: TOA: tan = opp/adj.

items.markingKey: In an isosceles right-angled triangle opposite = adjacent.

items.stem: In triangle ABC, angle B = 90°, angle A = 28° and the hypotenuse AC = 20 cm. Grace writes BC = 20 × cos 28° = 17.7 cm. Explain the error and find BC.
items.answer: BC is opposite angle A, so sine should be used: BC = 20 sin 28° = 9.39 cm.
items.markingKey: B1 BC is opposite A (not adjacent); M1 20 sin 28°; A1 9.39 cm [3]

items.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is 14.5 cm and one other side is 8 cm. Calculate the angle between the 8 cm side and the hypotenuse.
items.markingKey: M1 cos θ = 8/14.5; M1 inverse function; A1 56.5°.

items.markingKey: M1 cos θ = 8/10; M1 inverse function; A1 36.9°.

items.stem: A wheelchair ramp at a library in Mexico City rises 0.8 m over a horizontal distance of 8 m. (a) Calculate the angle the ramp makes with the horizontal. (b) The maximum safe angle is 4.8°. Calculate the least horizontal distance needed for a rise of 0.8 m.

Calculate the new distance from the wall.
An angle of elevation is measured
items.markingKey: Elevation: looking up from the horizontal line of sight.

items.stem: Explain why the angle of depression from A to B is equal to the angle of elevation from B to A.
items.answer: The horizontal lines at A and B are parallel, and the line AB is a transversal, so the two angles are alternate angles and are equal.
items.markingKey: B1 parallel horizontals; B1 alternate angles [2]

items.stem: A student measures an angle of depression from the vertical instead of the horizontal and gets 65°. Explain how to correct this.
items.answer: Angles of depression are measured from the horizontal, so the correct angle is 90° − 65° = 25°.
items.markingKey: B1 from the horizontal; B1 25° [2]

items.stem: A drone hovers 12 m above a point on level ground. Ethan stands 20 m from that point. Calculate the angle of elevation of the drone from Ethan's feet.
From the top of a cliff 72 m high, the angle of depression of a boat is 44°. Calculate the horizontal distance of the boat from the foot of the cliff.
items.markingKey: M1 angle of elevation from boat = 44°; M1 72 ÷ tan 44°; A1 74.6 m.

items.stem: A lighthouse on the coast near Jakarta has its light 75 m above sea level. From the light, the angles of depression of two boats P and Q, which are in a straight line with the foot of the lighthouse, are 36° and 31°. (a) Calculate the distance of P from the foot of the lighthouse. (b) Write down the angle of elevation of the light from boat Q, giving a reason.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 75 ÷ tan 36°; A1 103 [2] (b) B1 value; B1 reason [2]

items.stem: Explain why the height of an observer's eyes must be included when finding the height of a tree from an angle of elevation.
items.answer: The angle is measured from eye level, so the trigonometry gives the height above the eyes; the eye height must be added to get the height above the ground.
items.markingKey: B1 measured from eye level; B1 add eye height [2]

items.stem: From a point 50 m from the foot of a building the angle of elevation of the top is 35°. Daniel calculates the height as 50 × sin 35° = 28.7 m. Explain the error and find the correct height.
items.answer: The 50 m is the adjacent side and the height is opposite, so tan should be used: 50 tan 35° = 35.0 m.
items.markingKey: B1 should use tan (opp/adj); M1 50 tan 35°; A1 35.0 m [3]

items.stem: A drone hovers 12 m above a point on level ground. Chloe stands 64 m from that point. Calculate the angle of elevation of the drone from Chloe's feet.

Which is the sine rule for triangle ABC?
options: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
a sin A = b sin B
items.answer: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
items.markingKey: Each side over the sine of its opposite angle.

items.stem: Explain why the sine rule can give two possible triangles when finding an angle.
items.answer: sin θ = sin(180° − θ), so an acute angle and its obtuse supplement both have the same sine; both may fit the given information.
items.markingKey: B1 sin θ = sin(180 − θ); B1 two possible angles [2]

items.stem: Explain how the cosine rule a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A becomes Pythagoras' theorem when A = 90°.
items.answer: cos 90° = 0, so the term 2bc cos A disappears and a² = b² + c².
items.markingKey: B1 cos 90° = 0; B1 result [2]

items.markingKey: (a) M1 cos Q = (95² + QR² − 140²) ÷ (2 × 95 × QR) (or sine rule, checking for obtuse); A1 40.1° [2] (b) M1 140 sin 114° (or 2 × area ÷ 95); A1 128 m [2]

items.stem: A triangular plot of land PQR near Manila has PQ = 200 m, PR = 160 m and angle QPR = 120°. (a) Calculate the length of QR. (b) Calculate angle PQR.

items.stem: Which is the cosine rule for finding side a?
items.markingKey: Side a is opposite angle A, between sides b and c.

items.stem: Triangle PQR has PQ = 12 cm, PR = 9 cm and angle QPR = 150°. What is its area?
Explain why ½ab sin C is used rather than ½ × base × height when the height is not known.
items.answer: The height from the base b is a sin C, so ½ × b × a sin C gives the area without measuring the height.
items.markingKey: B1 h = a sin C; B1 substitution [2]

items.markingKey: The sine graph repeats every 360°.

items.stem: Explain why the equation sin x = 1.4 has no solutions.
items.answer: The value of sin x always lies between −1 and 1, so it can never equal 1.4.
items.markingKey: B1 range −1 to 1; B1 conclusion [2]

items.stem: Explain why cos x = −0.5 has two solutions between 0° and 360°.
items.answer: The cosine graph is below the x-axis between 90° and 270° and is symmetrical about x = 180°, so the line y = −0.5 crosses it twice: 120° and 240°.
items.markingKey: B1 graph symmetry/two crossings; B1 120° and 240° [2]

items.stem: Solve the equation tan x = 1.5 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
items.markingKey: M1 principal value tan⁻¹(1.5); M1 uses symmetry/period of the graph; A1 56.3° and 236.3°.

items.stem: A cuboid ABCDEFGH has a rectangular base ABCD with AB = 10 cm and BC = 4 cm, and height 3 cm. Calculate the length of the space diagonal AG.
items.markingKey: M1 AC² = 10² + 4²; M1 AG² = AC² + 3²; A1 11.2 cm.

items.stem: A square-based pyramid VABCD has base side 14 cm. The vertex V is vertically above the centre M of the base and VM = 15 cm. The pyramid is a model of a monument in Mexico City. (a) Calculate the length of the diagonal AC of the base. (b) Calculate the angle between VA and the base.
Explain how to find the angle between a space diagonal of a cuboid and its base.
items.answer: Find the diagonal of the base (Pythagoras), then use the right-angled triangle formed by the base diagonal, the vertical edge and the space diagonal: tan θ = height ÷ base diagonal.
items.markingKey: B1 base diagonal; B1 right-angled triangle with vertical edge [2]

items.stem: Amara solves sin x = −0.82 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360° and gives only the calculator answer x = -55.1°. Explain why this is not a complete (or correct) answer and find all the solutions.
items.answer: The calculator gives one value only and it is outside the range; the graph of y = sin x crosses y = −0.82 twice in this range: x = 235.1° and x = 304.9°.
items.markingKey: B1 explains second solution from graph symmetry/range; A1 235.1°; A1 304.9° [3]

items.stem: Solve the equation sin x = 0.35 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
items.markingKey: M1 principal value sin⁻¹(0.35); M1 uses symmetry/period of the graph; A1 20.5° and 159.5°.

items.markingKey: (a) M1 √(8² + 8²); A1 [2] (b) M1 uses midpoint of AB, distance 4 from M; M1 tan θ = 12/4; A1 71.6° [3]

items.markingKey: Back bearing: 070° + 180° = 250°.

items.stem: A map has a scale of 1 : 25,000. Freya says 3 cm on the map represents 75 m. Explain the mistake and find the correct distance in kilometres.

items.answer: Use the sine rule when you have a side and its opposite angle (a pair); use the cosine rule when you have two sides and the included angle, or all three sides.
items.markingKey: B1 sine rule condition; B1 cosine rule condition [2]

items.stem: In triangle ABC, b = 7 cm, c = 13 cm and angle A = 105°. Mateo says that because A is obtuse, cos A should be made positive, and calculates a² = 7² + 13² − 2 × 7 × 13 × 0.2588. Explain the error and find a.
items.answer: cos 105° is negative (−0.2588), and the sign must be kept, so −2bc cos A is added: a = 16.3 cm.
items.markingKey: B1 cos of obtuse angle is negative and must be used as it is; M1 a² = 7² + 13² − 2(7)(13)cos 105°; A1 16.3 cm [3]
